chunks: Shu'ayb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about garlic, onions, and leeks, so he said:
There is no harm in eating them raw and in pots, and there is no harm in seeking treatment with garlic. But when that is the case, then he should not go out to the mosque.

key_terms.الثُّومِ: garlic; mentioned as permissible to eat and use medicinally
key_terms.الْبَصَلِ: onions; included among the foods being asked about
key_terms.الْكُرَّاثِ: leeks; included with garlic and onions in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque; the place one is instructed not to go to after consuming such foods
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicates permissibility
key_terms.يُتَدَاوَى: to seek treatment; refers to using garlic medicinally

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat garlic or onions and then go to the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that eating garlic, onions, and leeks, whether raw or cooked, is permissible, and using garlic as a remedy is also permitted. However, it instructs a person not to go to the mosque after doing so, indicating concern for the sanctity of communal worship and avoiding offense to others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4268 - Shu'ayb narrated from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (as) was asked about garlic, onions, and leeks.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in eating them raw or cooked in pots, and there is no harm in using garlic as a remedy. However, if one does so, let him not go to the mosque."
